# Delivery contracts and recovery ownership

## Start with one representative question

[S04-Q019](#S04-Q019)

<p>How do queue and topic/subscription models differ in who should receive a message? Choose a model for distributing work and for notifying independent interested services.</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Choose a recipient model and define what happens to work when processing cannot finish.</p>

<ul>
<li>Choose queue or topic/subscription behavior from recipient requirements.</li>
<li>Trace broker decoupling, competing workers and a failed processing attempt.</li>
<li>Specify bounded retry, quarantine and accountable safe replay.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

No catalog prerequisite. Establish the terms and scenario assumptions in the foundation questions before progressing; a published lesson is not evidence that you know them.

<p>Begin with who must receive the work. Explain how a broker separates producer and consumer timing, then distribute attempts across workers. A failed attempt challenges that contract and leads to decisions about another attempt, quarantine and recovery ownership.</p>

### S04-Q019 · Foundation

<p>How do queue and topic/subscription models differ in who should receive a message? Choose a model for distributing work and for notifying independent interested services.</p>

> Explain queue versus topic/subscription models.

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain the recipient contract: one logical work item and several independently interested recipients are different requirements.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose a delivery model from recipient needs.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State the broker/version before claiming delivery or retention guarantees and check official documentation. Do not assume a model alone fixes redelivery behavior.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Describe recipients and subscription ownership for both examples.</li>
<li>Explain what happens to the requirement when a new independent consumer is added.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming every consumer attached to a queue receives its own copy of each message.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<li>Can different subscribers need different recovery policies?</li>

<a id="S04-Q021"></a>

### S04-Q021 · Mechanism

<p>How does a message broker decouple a producer from a consumer? Explain which dependencies are reduced and which agreements the two sides still share.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q021](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q021)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q021](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q021)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How do message brokers decouple producers and consumers?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Decoupling means reducing a particular dependency, such as simultaneous availability. It does not mean the consumer can ignore message meaning.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Identify the exact coupling changed by introducing a broker.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a generic producer/consumer pair; state delivery and storage assumptions instead of assuming a broker product.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Trace publishing and processing when the consumer is delayed.</li>
<li>Identify remaining schema, meaning and operational dependencies with a compatibility check.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Claiming that a broker eliminates all coupling between services.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you change a message contract without breaking existing consumers?</li>
<li>What happens to producers if broker capacity is exhausted?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q020"></a>

### S04-Q020 · Mechanism

<p>How do competing consumers share work, and what changes when you add worker replicas? Trace one message while a worker is processing it and another worker becomes available.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q020](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q020)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q020](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q020)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain competing consumers.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Competing consumers share a work stream rather than representing separate business subscribers. Explain distribution and responsibility for finishing an attempt.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reason about worker coordination during message delivery.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Specify broker/version and processing mode; consult official documentation for acknowledgment, locking and redelivery guarantees.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Separate work distribution from the business effect of processing.</li>
<li>Explain a worker-failure case and identify evidence needed to inspect ownership.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Equating more workers with a guarantee that each message has only one processing attempt.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What could happen if a worker loses its processing ownership?</li>
<li>Which resource might limit throughput after workers are added?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q022"></a>

### S04-Q022 · Failure cases

<p>What can happen after a message-processing attempt fails? Trace the message and any business changes for a failure before commit and a failure after commit but before acknowledgment.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q022](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q022)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q022](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q022)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What happens when a message processing attempt fails?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>An acknowledgment reports processing progress to the broker. Separating that report from business state exposes the uncertainty the question asks you to reason about.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Trace message and business-state outcomes across a failed attempt.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Choose broker/version and transaction boundaries. Check official delivery and acknowledgment documentation before stating the next delivery behavior.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Distinguish attempt failure from absence of a committed business effect.</li>
<li>Propose observations or failure injection for both interruption points.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming an exception proves that no business change was committed.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What if the worker cannot determine whether the commit succeeded?</li>
<li>Which state would a later attempt need to inspect?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S04-Q023"></a>

### S04-Q023 · Failure cases

<a id="S05-Q047"></a>

<p>How would you handle work that repeatedly fails, including retryable messages and poison messages? Explain when attempts should stop and how quarantined work can be investigated and recovered.</p>

**Source:** [S04-Q023](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q023) · [S05-Q047](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q047)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S04-Q023](../../sources/04-architecture-distributed-systems.md#q023)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain retry and dead-letter/poison-message handling.

</div>

**[S05-Q047](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q047)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What should happen to work that repeatedly fails?

</div>

**Why these source prompts share a canonical question:** Shared recovery policy for repeatedly failing work; retain retry and poison/dead-letter scope.

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>A poison message cannot currently be processed successfully; a dead-letter area holds work removed from normal delivery. Neither label alone defines a recovery process.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Design bounded retry and accountable recovery for failed work.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Preserve both source contexts: message handling and repeatedly failing background work. Specify provider/version and consult official retry/dead-letter documentation for concrete behavior.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Distinguish a transient failure from a persistent invalid input using evidence.</li>
<li>Assign investigation, safe replay and monitoring ownership.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating a dead-letter destination as successful completion or automatic recovery.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How do you avoid repeating side effects when replaying repaired work?</li>
<li>Which evidence would justify another attempt instead of quarantine?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>An import producer sends work that one worker should process while two independent services need completion notifications. Choose the recipient models. A malformed item repeatedly fails and a worker stops during another item: describe delivery observations, retry limits, investigation ownership and safe replay checks for the selected broker.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Distinguishes recipient models and recognizes that failed work needs an explicit next action.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Traces failure and redelivery, checks provider guarantees and defines recoverable retry/quarantine behavior with owners and tests.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>Queue names and retry counts without failure observations, provider scope or a replay procedure leave recovery unverified.</p>
